title: Negotiative Alignment: Embracing Disagreement to Achieve Fairer Outcomes – Insights from Urban Studies

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing street design evaluations (focusing on accessibility and practicality) and simulated LLM-agent utility outcomes between wheelchair users and other demographic groups to identify marginalized preferences.

Analyzing differences in street evaluations (such as security and liveliness) between senior and younger participants, and evaluating fairness metrics like worst-group utility in simulated multi-agent urban planning negotiations.

Comparing ratings of symbolic inclusion, aesthetics, and liveliness between LGBTQIA2+ participants and other demographic groups, and tracking utility outcomes for LGBTQIA2+ personas in LLM-mediated negotiations.
